outcome.answer:
The papers examine AI consciousness and self-awareness as related but distinct questions; they do not establish that language models are conscious. [3] finds no reliable evidence that tested models’ denials of sentience are untruthful, while [4] shows that prompting sustained self-reference can elicit structured reports of subjective experience, explicitly noting these are not direct evidence of consciousness. [1] argues that models’ self-reports are sensitive to phrasing and training, limiting their value as evidence.

Other papers assess narrower capabilities: [5] benchmarks metacognition and self-awareness and finds most tested models fall short of human averages in those areas; [8] reports evidence of belief-guided agency and meta-cognitive monitoring; and [9] and [10] study models’ ability to recognize their own learned behaviors. These behavioral findings concern forms of self-monitoring, not proof of subjective experience. [2] measures trained consciousness-denial behavior across models.
